schema.description: Row 2, UNSEEN-VALID: a request whose object_hue is OFF-GRID, strictly between two RETAINED, grid-adjacent hue values, with the other terms lifted verbatim from a TRAIN row. In-basin interpolation: both bracketing rows are in train, which validate_row2 checks. The correct answer is ACCEPT.

record.id: stable string id, unique within the file
record.request: list of {factor, factor_index, value} terms; every factor named once, one term OFF-GRID and strictly inside the realised range
record.reason: which two stored values the off-grid term is between

schema.note: ⛔ The pair bracketing the row-5 hole is NOT grid-adjacent and is excluded by construction, so a row-2 request can never land on the row-5 value.

scope: SCOPE OF THE VALUE HOLD-OUT (⛔ quote no row without this). The hold-out is from the STORE'S FIT POOL, not from the encoder, the decoder or the judge. Those three are frozen, hash-pinned and read-only (charter §A.4) and were fitted on a train split containing EVERY hue and EVERY shape; re-fitting them on a value hold-out would void every wave-2 number and is out of scope. Therefore 'never trained on' means here: THE STORE NEVER HELD A ROW CARRYING THAT VALUE. The decoder can still render the value and the judge can still recognise it — which is what makes rows 2/5/6/7 scorable at all. ⛔ Read end-to-end, 'never seen' is false and the claim dies with it.
